January
A Dutch pilot spots people paddling canoes on lakes high in the mountains of West New Guinea, a region thought to be empty. The discovery sparks new mission efforts.
January

Vedanayagam Samuel Azariah, the first Indian-born Anglican bishop in India, dies. In Dornakal, one of India's poorest regions, the church grew from about 8,000 believers to roughly 300,000 under his leadership.
January
Severinus, a missionary from Africa who preached along the Danube River, dies in his monastic cell in what is now Austria.
January
Moravian missionaries and Khoikhoi believers dedicate a church seating 1,500 at Genadendal, South Africa.
January
Harriet Bedell dies in Florida after years as an Episcopal missionary among Native Americans in Oklahoma, Alaska, and Florida.
January
Hilda Stumpf, an elderly missionary with the Africa Inland Mission who had opposed female circumcision, is murdered in Kenya.
January
Isabella Thoburn arrives in India, where she will become a leading missionary educator of women.
January
Chief Arabina, the first believer among the Saramaccan people of Suriname, is baptized by Moravian missionaries.
January
The Swedish Mission Society is founded.
January
Presbyterian missionary Edith Warner sets out from Asaba, Nigeria, becoming the first white woman to visit the East Niger region.
January
Cyrus Hamlin, future missionary to Turkey and founder of Robert College in Constantinople, is born.
January
Kate Youngman and Mary Park open Graham Seminary in Tokyo, Japan. Youngman later serves people with leprosy.
January
Pliny Fisk reaches Smyrna and begins missionary travels across the Middle East, handing out thousands of Bibles, Scripture portions, and tracts.
January
Canadian missionary Alice Wood arrives in Argentina, where she helps plant one of the first lasting Pentecostal works in Buenos Aires.
January
Lillian Dickson, founder of The Mustard Seed relief and mission agency, dies in Taiwan.
January
John Horden, Anglican missionary to Canada's First Nations and first bishop of Moosonee, dies. He had learned five Indigenous languages.
January
Henry Venn, mission strategist of the Church Missionary Society who urged self-governing, self-supporting, self-propagating churches, dies in England.
January
John Roberts, missionary to the Shoshone and Arapaho of Wyoming who translated Scripture into both of their languages, dies.
January
Lutheran missionary Bartholomäus Ziegenbalg debates Tamil Hindus at Tranquebar, India, about whether all religions lead to God.
January
A British ship reaches Banner Cove, Patagonia, and finds Allen Gardiner and his missionary team dead of starvation. Their diaries show they sang hymns to the end.
January
The Finnish Missionary Society is founded.
January
Revival breaks out at a Bible seminary in Ngouedi, Republic of the Congo, after Swedish missionaries and Congolese believers had prayed for an outpouring of the Holy Spirit.
January
Clara Clerget (Sister Anne-Marie), a French nun who served people with leprosy in Madagascar for more than fifty years, dies.
January
Louisa Stead, missionary and writer of the hymn “’Tis So Sweet to Trust in Jesus,” dies in Southern Rhodesia (Zimbabwe).
January
Christian Friedrich Schwartz sails from London for Tranquebar, India. He will serve there for nearly fifty years.
January
Baptist missionaries John Chamberlain and H. Peacock leave Serampore to start a mission in Agra, India, 800 miles away.
January
Fanny Jackson Coppin, a former slave who became an educator and a missionary to South Africa, dies.
January
John R. Mott, leader of the Student Volunteer Movement and the 1910 Edinburgh World Missionary Conference, dies.
January
Oswald J. Smith, missions champion and founder of The Peoples Church in Toronto, dies. He raised millions of dollars for world missions.
January
Sarah Doremus, called the “Mother of Missions” for her work rallying women to support foreign missions, dies.
January
Sarah Lanman Huntington Smith arrives in Beirut, where she will serve Syrian women as a missionary.
January
John G. Paton, missionary to the New Hebrides (Vanuatu), dies. Early in his ministry he buried his wife and infant son with his own hands.
January
John Williams, future missionary to the South Pacific, comes to faith in Christ.
February
Anne-Marie Javouhey sails from France for Senegal as a missionary. Her work will reach both Africa and South America.
February
Bishop Walter Lambuth and Dr. John Gilbert reach the village of Chief Wembo-Niama in the Belgian Congo to choose a site for a mission station.
February
Adoniram Judson, Samuel Newell, Samuel Nott, Gordon Hall, and Luther Rice are commissioned in Salem, Massachusetts, as America's first foreign missionaries.
February
Daniel Olubi is ordained an Anglican priest in Nigeria. He will become a key leader in spreading the gospel among the Yoruba.
February
Ann Hasseltine Judson and Harriet Atwood Newell are commissioned in Haverhill, Massachusetts, as missionaries to India.
February
Twelve American missionaries, including Daniel Lindley, get their first sight of Africa from the deck of their ship.
February
Claudius Buchanan dies in England. As a chaplain in India, he worked to free missionaries from the control of the East India Company.
February
John James Ransom, the first Southern Methodist missionary to Brazil, arrives in Rio de Janeiro.
February
Macedonian rebels release Ellen Stone, an American missionary to Turkey, after holding her for ransom for five months.
February
Daniel Bliss arrives in Syria, beginning nearly fifty years of service that will include founding what becomes the American University of Beirut.
February
William Henry Brett, who spent forty years in mission and language work in British Guiana (Guyana), dies.
February
Archbishop Simon of Shanghai and Beijing dies. The Orthodox mission in China grew significantly under his leadership.
February
The last hostile soldiers leave the Nazarene mission at Tavane, Mozambique, in ruins. Pastor Benjamin Langa had kept preaching even with guns pointed at him.
February
Christian Friedrich Schwartz, called the “Apostle of India,” dies in Tanjore after nearly fifty years of service.
February
Devadasen and three other Indian believers are ordained in Nagercoil, the first ordinations of the Travancore Mission.
February
Minnie Cumming Watson, the first woman missionary of the East Africa Scottish Mission, dies. She built a network of Christian schools among the Kikuyu of Kenya.
February
Ji Zhiwen, Chinese evangelist who founded the Bethel Evangelistic Band and later planted churches in Taiwan and Southeast Asia, dies.
February
Levi Parsons arrives in Jerusalem, the first Protestant missionary to establish a permanent mission there.
February
John “Praying” Hyde, missionary to India known for his nights of intercession, dies. His last words: “Shout the victory of Jesus Christ!”
February
Koilas Chunder Mookerjee, a young Hindu convert who shared Christ with fellow Indians despite persecution, dies of cholera in Calcutta.
February
Samuel and Catherine Leigh sail into a New Zealand bay to begin Methodist work among the Maori.
February
James Gilmour sails from Liverpool for China and Mongolia. On the voyage he shares the gospel with every member of the crew.
February
Charles and Lettie Cowman arrive in Japan, where they will cofound the Oriental Missionary Society (now One Mission Society).
February
The ship Caravan sails from Salem, Massachusetts, carrying the Judsons and the Newells, America's first foreign missionaries.
February
Bartholomäus Ziegenbalg dies in Tranquebar, India, at thirty-six. He had translated the New Testament into Tamil and baptized more than two hundred people.
February
Moravian missionaries and believers dedicate a new church at Friedensthal on St. Croix. The crowd is so large that most cannot fit inside.
February
Lucy Peabody and Helen Montgomery lead women in a day of prayer for missions. It grows into an annual worldwide prayer day.
February
William M. Strong, founder of the Gospel Mission of South America, dies.
February
Missionary Jean-Pierre Néel and four Chinese believers are executed in Guizhou, China, for refusing to deny their faith.
February
A mob attacks the Presbyterian mission at Yeung Kong, China, looting the homes of two missionary families.
February
Stanley Frodsham honors Paul Bettex, a Swiss-born missionary who had been killed and secretly buried in China fourteen years earlier.
February
Joel Gamonal comes to Christ in Peru. He will become a church planter with HeartCry Missionary Society.
March
Khasi believers in Assam, India, are moved to tears during a service on the Holy Spirit, and revival spreads through the region.
March
Filipino missionary Gaspar Makil, his young daughter Janie, and American missionary Elwood Jacobson are killed by the Viet Cong in Vietnam.
March
Johannes van der Kemp, missionary to South Africa, arrives in Cape Town. He will use his own money to free many slaves.
March
Fidelia Fiske sails from Boston for Persia by way of Smyrna, asking her sisters to pray for her because her usefulness may depend on their prayers.
February
François Coillard and Christina Mackintosh marry in Cape Town, beginning decades of shared missionary work in southern Africa.
February
Lucy Peabody, who poured her life and fortune into world missions, dies in Danvers, Massachusetts.
March
Missionary John Luther Stephens is murdered by a mob in Ahualulco, Mexico, where he had been teaching night classes and preaching.
March
A mob attacks the home of Adventist missionary Frederick Stahl near Lake Titicaca, Peru, and beats teacher Manuel Camacho.
February
Henry Williams reaches Sydney on his way to New Zealand, where he will lead the Church Missionary Society's work among the Maori.
March
Samuel Zwemer, future “Apostle to Islam,” preaches his first sermon in a small church in New Brunswick, New Jersey.
March
Mary Ann Thomson, writer of the missions hymn “O Zion, Haste,” dies in Philadelphia.
March
Melville Cox arrives in Liberia as the first Methodist missionary to Africa. He dies within four months, and his courage stirs a wave of missionary zeal.
March
Mamiyeri Gwambe is baptized in South Africa, taking the name Bernard Mizeki. He will serve as a missionary in Zimbabwe and be martyred there ten years later.
March
William Arthur, Methodist missionary to India and author, dies in Cannes, France.
March
William Ward, mission printer and coworker of William Carey at Serampore, dies in Calcutta.
March
Pope Gregory the Great dies. He sent Augustine and a team of monks to bring the gospel to the Anglo-Saxons of England.
March
Pennsylvania militiamen massacre ninety-six peaceful Christian Lenape at the Moravian mission of Gnadenhütten, Ohio.
March
James Calvert, Methodist pioneer missionary to Fiji, dies in England.
March
Henry Nott and his fellow missionaries hold the first Christian service in Tahiti, under great trees, with the king present.
March
Adalbert of Bremen, archbishop and missionary leader to Scandinavia, dies.
March
Japanese forces separate missionaries Russell and Darlene Deibler in the Dutch East Indies. His last words to her: God will never leave or forsake them. He dies in a prison camp.
March
Yusuf Jatau, Hausa-language radio preacher and fifty-year mission leader of the Nigerian Baptist Convention, dies.
March
Eusebio Kino, Jesuit missionary and explorer among the Pima people of Arizona and northern Mexico, dies.
March
Antoine Daniel sails for New France, where he will be one of eight Jesuit missionaries martyred.
March
Friedrich Schmid opens a center near Ann Arbor, Michigan, to train missionaries to Native Americans.
March
Ida Scudder's first class of women doctors graduates in Vellore, India. Her school will grow into one of Asia's leading medical centers.
March
The first Jesuit missionaries to Peru arrive at Callao.
March
William Christie sails for Tibet, writing that he will “spend and be spent” for his Savior. He becomes known as the “Apostle of Tibet.”
March
Robert Wilder, a founder of the Student Volunteer Movement and its watchword, “the evangelization of the world in this generation,” dies in Norway.
March
Alexander Merensky, missionary to the Transvaal in South Africa, dies in Berlin.
March
George S. Fisher, founder of the Gospel Missionary Union, dies of typhoid in Guayaquil, Ecuador, while visiting the work there.
March
James, a former Hindu who led a string of Christian schools and shared the gospel with his own people, dies in Bankura, India.
March
Missionary Lynda Bethea is beaten to death by robbers in Kenya after she and her husband stop to help a man lying in the road.
March
Methodist women in Boston organize the Woman's Foreign Missionary Society.
March
Paris Reidhead, missionary to Sudan and preacher of “Ten Shekels and a Shirt,” dies.
April
David Brainerd arrives at Kaunaumeek, Massachusetts, to serve among the Mahican people.
April
Baptist missionary Jonathan Goble arrives in Japan. He later invents a cart for his ailing wife that becomes the rickshaw.
April
Solomon Ginsburg, missionary to Brazil, dies in São Paulo.
April
Boers force François Coillard out of his mission station in the Orange Free State.
April
Samuel Zwemer, the “Apostle to Islam,” dies in New York.
March
James Lloyd Breck, Episcopal frontier missionary, dies in California.
March
Innocent Veniaminov, Russian Orthodox missionary to Alaska who created a written language for the Aleut people, dies in Moscow.
March
Moravian missionary Karl Bregenzer is murdered by rebels in Nicaragua. His family survives by hiding in the forest.
April
Charles Freer Andrews, Anglican missionary to India and friend of Mahatma Gandhi, dies in Calcutta.
April
The French Canadian Missionary Society is formed to bring the gospel to French speakers in Canada.
April
Mahay Choramo dies in Ethiopia. He carried the gospel across the Omo region and endured many beatings and imprisonments.
April
Franciscan Thomas of Tolentino and his companions are killed near Bombay, India. They become known as the Four Martyrs of Thane.
April
Moravian missionaries and Khoikhoi believers begin a new mission at the Witte River in South Africa. It is destroyed the next year, but a stronger station is rebuilt nearby.
April
Moravian missionaries David Zeisberger and John Heckewelder are brought to Fort Detroit and tried for treason. They are found not guilty.
April
Sarah Doremus becomes the first president of the Woman's Union Missionary Society, the first American women's mission board.
April
Betty Greene, World War II pilot and cofounder of Mission Aviation Fellowship, dies in Seattle.
April
Methodius dies. With his brother Cyril, he brought the gospel and a written alphabet to the Slavic peoples.
April
William M. Thomson, longtime missionary to Syria and author of The Land and the Book, dies in Denver.
April
Moved by the preaching of Jesuit Antonio de Andrade, the king of Guge in Tibet lays the cornerstone of Tibet's first church.
April
Presbyterian missionary Ashbel Green Simonton starts his first Sunday school in Brazil.
April
Johanna Veenstra, Christian Reformed missionary to Nigeria, dies in Jos.
April
Methodist missionary Willis Hoover leaves his church in Valparaíso, Chile, and soon leads the new Pentecostal Methodist Church, the start of a major Chilean revival movement.
April
Lettie Cowman, missionary to Japan, cofounder of the Oriental Missionary Society, and author of Streams in the Desert, dies.
April
Missionary Jean-André Soulié is executed in Tibet after eleven days of torture.
April
Nine hundred Sunday school children gather in Beirut to honor Sarah Huntington Smith, who started girls' education there fifty-nine years earlier.
April
Eduard Arndt, pioneer Lutheran missionary to China, dies in Hankow.
April
Alexander Worthy Clerk, a Jamaican, arrives in the Gold Coast (Ghana) with other Jamaican believers to serve as missionaries.
April
Assemblies of God missionary Frank Isensee dies in an accident while traveling to bring the gospel to a city in Peru.
April
Medical missionary Wilfred Grenfell nearly dies when the ice pan he is on drifts out to sea off Newfoundland.
April
Rudolf Stoll, pioneer Moravian missionary in Suriname, dies.
April
John Marrant, African American missionary to Native Americans and Black Loyalists in Nova Scotia, dies in London.
April
Dayuma, the Waorani woman whose faith opened the way for the gospel among her people, is baptized at Wheaton College.
April
Adalbert of Prague is martyred while bringing the gospel to the Prussians.
April
Christian and Missionary Alliance pilot Albert Lewis dies in a crash near the Baliem Valley of New Guinea.
April
Nurse Wanda Fricke arrives in New Guinea to open a Lutheran medical mission.
April
German missionary Ernst Faber arrives in Hong Kong, where he will help Chinese believers write Christian books.
April
Jean de Brébeuf sails for New France, where he will serve the Huron people until his martyrdom.
April
Asahel Grant, pioneer missionary physician to the Nestorian Christians of Persia, dies in Mosul.
April
Protestant missionaries in the Philippines meet to form the Evangelical Union to advance the gospel across the islands.
May
Samuel Leigh, the first Methodist missionary to Australia, dies in England.
April
Marguerite Bourgeoys opens a school in Ville-Marie (Montreal), founding an uncloistered missionary community of women in New France.
April
A Fijian chief on Viwa declares that drums once used to announce human sacrifice will now call people to worship God, to the joy of missionary James Calvert.
April
Nlemvo becomes the first Protestant convert in the Congo. He will help translate the New Testament into Kikongo.
May
Dutch missionary George Candidius lands on Formosa (Taiwan) and begins learning the language and preaching.
May
Thomas Coke, Methodist leader and father of Methodist missions, dies at sea while leading a missionary team to India and Ceylon.
May
Five thousand Dani people in Papua gather for a two-day feast to celebrate receiving the New Testament in their own language.
May
Demetrius Gallitzin, Catholic missionary known as the “Apostle of the Alleghenies,” dies in Loretto, Pennsylvania.
May
Bandits attack Qinzhou, China, and kill Dr. Wu Baoying, a Christian doctor who founded the local hospital after serving with the China Inland Mission. His last words: “The Lord is with us.”
May
Ella Schenck and other United Brethren missionaries are captured and killed while fleeing an uprising in Rotifunk, Sierra Leone.
May
Ralph Darby Williams, Assemblies of God missionary who spent his life equipping believers in South and Central America, dies.
May
John Veniaminov leaves Irkutsk for Alaska, where he will translate Scripture into Indigenous languages.
May
Guido Verbeck sails for Japan, where his teaching and translation work will earn him the Order of the Rising Sun.
May
Moravian missionary David Zeisberger starts a mission among the Lenape at Fairfield, in what is now Ontario, Canada.
May
Church leaders meeting in New York City resolve to form the American Bible Society.
May
Columba and twelve companions land on Iona in a hide-covered boat. Iona becomes a base for evangelizing Scotland and northern England.
May
Samuel Marsden, the missionary chaplain called the “Apostle of New Zealand,” dies in New South Wales.
May
Huang Su'e, Chinese missionary educator who championed girls' education and rescued abandoned baby girls, dies.
May
Jim Broomhall, medical missionary to the Nosu (Yi) people of China and later to the Philippines, dies.
May
Annie Armstrong helps found the Woman's Missionary Union of the Southern Baptist Convention. The Easter offering for North American missions now bears her name.
May
Moravian believers dedicate a church at New Eden, Jamaica. Built for 500, it cannot hold the 900 who come.
May
Althea Brown is commissioned as a missionary to the Congo. She will compile a dictionary and grammar of the Bushong language.
May
Catherine Leigh, wife of pioneer Methodist missionary Samuel Leigh, dies after caring for the sick during an epidemic in Parramatta, Australia.
May
Presbyterian missionary Ashbel Green Simonton holds his first service in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.
May
Jacques Marquette, Jesuit missionary and explorer of the Mississippi, dies in Michigan.
May
Macarius Glukharev, who founded a fruitful Orthodox mission among the Altai people of Siberia, dies.
May
Jeremiah Kisula is baptized. He will become the first bishop of the Africa Inland Church in Tanzania, known as a man of prayer and a church planter.
May
Joseph Bullen meets Chickasaw leader Levi Colbert in Mississippi to propose a mission to the Chickasaw. The idea is welcomed.
May
Jonas King, missionary to Greece and gifted linguist, dies in Athens.
May
John Eliot, missionary to the Algonquin peoples of New England, dies. His Algonquin Bible was the first Bible printed in America.
May
The Christian Airmen's Missionary Fellowship, later Mission Aviation Fellowship, is founded.
May
Pierre-Jean De Smet, Jesuit missionary to Native peoples of the American West, dies in St. Louis.
May
Henry Blodget, who served forty years in China and helped translate the Mandarin New Testament, dies.
May
Ludwig Nommensen, Lutheran missionary to the Batak people of Sumatra, dies.
May
John Ryland, who helped William Carey organize the Baptist Missionary Society, dies in Bristol.
May
Lillian May Thomas, an African American missionary, sails for the Congo.
May
Missionary Gustave Behr is murdered near a monastery in Batang, Tibet.
May
Willis Hoover, Methodist missionary who helped start Chile's Pentecostal movement, dies in Valparaíso.
May
Florence Young, founder of the Queensland Kanaka Mission (later the South Sea Evangelical Mission), dies in Sydney.
May
Mary Webb dies in Boston. Despite needing a wheelchair from childhood, she founded one of America's first women's missionary societies.
May
Jackson Kemper, Episcopal missionary bishop to the American frontier, dies in Wisconsin.
May
George Burder, a founder of the London Missionary Society and the British and Foreign Bible Society, dies in London.
May
Samuel Zwemer is ordained in the Reformed Church in America.
May
Hubert, the “Apostle of the Ardennes,” dies.
May
Reginald Heber writes the missionary hymn “From Greenland's Icy Mountains.”
May
Barbara Johnston is filled with the Spirit. The next year she sails as Canada's first Pentecostal missionary to India.
June
John Scudder and three other missionary couples sail from Boston for India. Scudder is the first American medical missionary.
June
Newlyweds Samuel and Marie Gobat leave Germany for Ethiopia as missionaries.
June
Sheikh Salih is baptized as Abdul Masih after reading Henry Martyn's Hindustani New Testament while binding its pages. He becomes a bold witness among Muslims.
June
Azariah Smith, missionary doctor to Armenians in Turkey, dies.
June
Arthur Tappan Pierson, missions advocate and revival leader, dies.
June
Ji Wang is secretly baptized in Taiwan. By her death, five thousand of the Truku people will be baptized through her ministry.
June
Pope Gregory XV creates the Congregation for the Propagation of the Faith to direct Catholic missions worldwide.
June
Anna Hinderer, missionary to the Yoruba of Nigeria, dies in England.
June
Harold Wildish sails for South America after God answers his prayer for passage money to the exact amount.
June
Aaron of Cuddalore, the first Indian pastor ordained by the Lutheran mission at Tranquebar, dies after winning hundreds to Christ.
June
Missionary David Campbell, his wife, and their two children are killed during the Indian Rebellion.
June
Rimbert, archbishop of Hamburg-Bremen who helped evangelize Scandinavia, dies.
June
Samuel J. Mills dies at sea after scouting West Africa for a mission site. He was a leader of the Haystack Prayer Meeting.
June
Twelve hundred people attend the dedication of the first Methodist chapel at Cape Coast, Ghana. Missionary Thomas Birch Freeman preaches.
June
Kwame Bediako, Ghanaian theologian of mission and founder of the Akrofi-Christaller Institute, dies.
June
Eusebio Kino is ordained a Jesuit priest. He will serve as a missionary in northern Mexico and Arizona.
June
David Brainerd is ordained in New Jersey for missionary work among Native Americans.
June
Dr. Divie Bethune McCartee, the first American Presbyterian missionary in central China, arrives at Ningbo.
June
Columba of Iona, missionary to Scotland, dies.
June
José de Anchieta, Jesuit missionary to Brazil who helped found São Paulo and Rio de Janeiro, dies.
June
Roland Allen, whose book Missionary Methods called for churches led by local believers from the start, dies in Nairobi.
June
Alice Clarissa Whitman, two-year-old daughter of missionaries Marcus and Narcissa Whitman, drowns in Oregon country.
June
Dan Beach Bradley, pioneer medical missionary to Thailand, dies in Bangkok.
June
Walter Ciszek is arrested in the Soviet Union for ministering in secret. He will spend twenty-three years in prisons and labor camps.
June
J. H. Bavinck, Dutch missionary to Indonesia and teacher of missions, dies.
June
Celina de Albuquerque is filled with the Spirit under the ministry of Swedish missionaries Daniel Berg and Gunnar Vingren, the first such event in Brazil's Pentecostal movement.
June
Nikolai Kasatkin, future Orthodox missionary to Japan, becomes a monk.
June
An imperial decree orders the killing of foreigners in China. Missionaries and Chinese Christians suffer most in the Boxer Uprising.
June
Poonamallee Rajahgopaul and A. Venkataramiah are baptized, the first converts of the Free Church mission in Madras, India.
June
Moravian missionaries arrive in Alaska to found the Bethel mission. John Henry Kilbuck will learn the Yup'ik language.
June
Jean de Brébeuf arrives in Quebec. He will be martyred while serving the Huron people.
June
Onesimos Nesib, Ethiopian evangelist who translated the Bible into Oromo, dies.
June
Isaac McCoy, Baptist missionary to Native Americans, dies.
June
Count Zinzendorf allows exiled Moravians to settle on his estate. Herrnhut becomes the base of the Moravian missionary movement.
June
James Theodore Holly is ordained a deacon in Detroit. He will become the Episcopal Church's first African American missionary bishop, serving in Haiti.
June
Lim Ang is baptized in Taiwan after hearing the gospel at a mission hospital. He becomes a beloved preacher.
June
Cyrus Kingsbury, missionary to the Cherokee and Choctaw peoples, dies.
June
Wilfred Grenfell launches the Strathcona, the mission boat for his medical work in Labrador.
June
Bruce Kennedy, Alaska Airlines leader who helped expand Mission Aviation Fellowship, dies in a plane crash.
June
Ludwig Nommensen lands on Sumatra to begin his work among the Batak people.
June
Myrtle Wilson and a group of women called to Africa pray for travel money. Within a month they have enough to sail.
July
Sarah and Grover Comstock sail from Boston for Burma. Sarah's kindness is so remembered that her death nine years later leads several Burmese to Christ.
July
Mary Webb is baptized in Boston. Though she uses a wheelchair, she will become a leading organizer of women's mission societies.
July
Missionary Horace Tracy Pitkin is beheaded at Baoding during the Boxer Uprising.
June
Bishop Nestor of Alaska, who translated the Gospels into an Alaskan language, drowns while returning from a visit to his remote churches.
June
Luis Bush, who coined the term “10/40 Window” for the least-reached region of the world, serves as senior consultant to the Global Consultation on World Evangelization in Pretoria, South Africa.
June
Raymond Lull, missionary to Muslims in North Africa, is stoned in Bougie (Béjaïa) and dies of his wounds.
June
John Beck, born to missionaries in Greenland, returns there after his studies. He will serve as a Moravian missionary in Greenland for more than fifty years.
June
Pastor Meng is beheaded at Baoding, China, after refusing to flee and abandon the missionaries.
July
Allen Gardiner founds the Patagonian Missionary Society. He will die in its service.
July
Missionary Dan Beach Bradley starts the Bangkok Recorder, the first newspaper in Thailand.
July
Twenty Mexicans led to Christ by teenager Henry C. Ball are baptized in Kingsville, Texas. Ball will go on to lead the Assemblies of God's Latin American work.
July
Hormazdji Pestonji, a Parsi convert who suffered for his faith, is baptized in Bombay. He will serve as a missionary in Poona.
July
Salvation Army officer Charles Péan sails for the penal colony on Devil's Island, French Guiana.
July
Hans Egede, the “Apostle of Greenland,” lands in Greenland with his family and a party of forty-six.
July
Calista Vinton sails for Burma, where she will write most of the hymns in the Sgaw Karen hymnal.
July
Samuel Schereschewsky is ordained a deacon in New York. He will serve as a missionary bishop and Bible translator in China.
July
J. A. Strain, F. W. Farnol, and George Fisher of the Gospel Missionary Union arrive in Ecuador, the first faith mission to enter the country.
July
The first Hawaiian missionaries sail for the Caroline Islands, carrying a letter from King Kamehameha III urging Pacific chiefs to welcome them.
July
Junípero Serra founds the first of nine California missions at San Diego.
July
Robert Morrison baptizes Cai Gao in Macau, his first Chinese convert after seven years of work.
July
Moravians celebrate fifty years of mission on St. John in the Virgin Islands, where 16,900 people have been baptized.
July
Boxers behead “Blind Chang” in Manchuria. He had won hundreds to Christ and gave himself up so that fifty other believers could go free.
July
Swedish missionary Gustaf Tornvall is killed by renegade soldiers in China while overseeing famine relief work.
July
Lal Behari Day is baptized in Calcutta. He will become a pastor, missionary, and author.
July
William Henry Brett is ordained in British Guiana. He will translate Scripture into Arawak and other local languages.
July
Melville Cox, the first Methodist missionary sent from America, dies of fever in Liberia. He had said, “Let a thousand fall before Africa be given up.”
July
Missionary nurse Josephine Desmond is killed at Quzhou, China, during the Boxer Uprising.
July
Moravian Johann Rüffer dies in Egypt after a dangerous attempt to take the gospel to Persia, during which he was robbed three times.
July
Bible distributor Francisco Penzotti is jailed in Peru for spreading Protestant faith. During his imprisonment he leads many prisoners to Christ, and the outcry helps open Peru to religious freedom.
July
Francis Pfanner lands in South Africa to begin the Mariannhill mission.
August
Henry Williams arrives in New Zealand, where he will lead the Church Missionary Society's work among the Maori.
August
Robert Morrison, the first Protestant missionary to China and translator of the Chinese Bible, dies in Canton.
July
The English Parliament passes an act to fund the spread of the gospel in New England, inspired by John Eliot's work among Native Americans.
July
John Sergeant, missionary to the Mahican people of Stockbridge, Massachusetts, dies.
July
William Wade Harris sets out to preach in the Ivory Coast. Tens of thousands come to faith through his ministry.
August
Fredrik Franson, founder of The Evangelical Alliance Mission (TEAM), dies.
July
Robert Jaffray, Christian and Missionary Alliance leader in China and Southeast Asia, dies in a Japanese prison camp.
August
Cyrus Hamlin, missionary to Turkey and founder of Robert College, dies in Portland, Maine.
August
Karl Gützlaff, pioneer missionary to China, dies in Hong Kong.
August
Minnie Janofski dies. As a widow she served missionaries in Bolivia for twenty-four years, cooking and sewing for them.
August
John Eliot, future missionary to the Algonquin peoples, is baptized in England.
August
Mary Slessor sails from Liverpool for Calabar, Nigeria.
August
Raymond Lull, in his eighties, sails for North Africa on his last mission to Muslims.
August
Stephen and Mary Riggs, missionaries to the Dakota, hold their last service at Hazelwood before war forces them to flee.
August
Bautista Silva, the first believer among the Piaroa people of Venezuela, dies. He helped translate the Bible and walked for miles to tell others about Jesus.
August
A revival in Lagos, Nigeria, begins. Among those converted is Adeline Omojola, who will help found the Women's Missionary Union of the Nigerian Baptist Convention.
August
Missionary James Stewart arrives in Cape Town. He will lead the Lovedale mission school.
August
Missionaries Edith Nathan, May Nathan, and Mary Heysman are captured by Boxers in Daning, China, and killed the next morning.
August
A group of Ayoré people in Bolivia lay down their weapons and come out of the jungle to meet New Tribes missionaries, four years after Ayoré warriors killed five missionaries.
August
Adam Schall, Jesuit missionary to China, dies. An earthquake had spared him from execution the year before.
August
Rebel soldiers take over the mission hospital at Nebobongo, Congo, holding Dr. Helen Roseveare captive for five months.
August
Cameron Townsend leaves home for Guatemala. He will found Wycliffe Bible Translators.
August
Russell and Darlene Deibler arrive in Batavia, Java, on their first wedding anniversary, on their way to serve in New Guinea.
August
John Sung, Chinese evangelist who preached across China and Southeast Asia, dies.
August
Gideon Blackburn, missionary to the Cherokee and frontier church planter, dies.
August
Huang Su'e marries missionary educator Francis Lister Hawks Pott in Shanghai.
August
Count Zinzendorf lays hands on Leonhard Dober and David Nitschmann, commissioning them as the first Moravian missionaries.
August
Missionary James Williamson is murdered by robbers on his boat in China.
August
Mildred Cable and Eva and Francesca French, the “Trio” of the Gobi Desert, are ordered to leave Suzhou, China.
August
Pitambar Singh, an Indian convert who became a writer and evangelist after reading a Serampore tract, dies.
August
Althea Brown sails for the Congo as a missionary.
August
Robert McDonald, Anglican missionary and linguist to the Gwich'in people of the Canadian Arctic, dies in Winnipeg.
August
Kenneth Pike crosses into Mexico as a missionary. He will become a groundbreaking linguist with Wycliffe and SIL.
September
Jean de Brébeuf baptizes the first Iroquois believer, a Seneca chief.
September
François Coillard sails for Cape Town, setting aside scholarly ambitions to serve in Africa.
September
Missionaries Marcus Whitman and Henry Spalding reach Walla Walla with their wives. Narcissa Whitman and Eliza Spalding are the first white women known to cross the continent overland.
September
Isabella Thoburn, missionary educator to the women of India, dies of cholera.
August
Aidan of Lindisfarne, the Irish missionary who brought the gospel to Northumbria, dies.
August
Raymond Nonnatus, who ransomed captives and sought to win Muslims to Christ, dies.
August
John Sergeant is ordained as a missionary to the Mahican people.
August
Boxers kill missionaries Willie and Helen Peat, their children, and their coworkers in Shanxi, China.
September
Isobel Kuhn enrolls at Moody Bible Institute to prepare for missionary service.
September
The KGB arrests Vasily Boyechko of the Good Samaritan Mission. In prison he leads fellow inmates to Christ.
September
David Abeel, pioneer missionary to Southeast Asia and China who helped start the Society for Promoting Female Education in the East, dies.
August
Peter Ambuofa, a Solomon Islander, is baptized in Queensland. Two years later he returns home to preach, and by 1904 has led two hundred people to Christ.
September
Robert Morrison reaches Canton, China, where he will translate the Bible into Chinese.
September
The cornerstone is laid for Ida Scudder's mission hospital in Vellore, India.
September
Luigi Francescon, Italian Pentecostal pioneer who helped start churches in Argentina, Brazil, and the United States, dies in Chicago.
September
Swedish missionary Anna-Greta Stjärne is shot and killed by bandits in Ethiopia.
September
Jacques-Désiré Laval, missionary to Mauritius, dies. The anniversary is a national holiday there.
September
Francis Asbury, sailing to America as a Methodist missionary, writes that he is not going for honor or money but to live for God and bring others to do the same.
September
Presbyterian missionary William Newton Blair arrives in Korea, where he will witness the great revival of 1907.
September
Chilean Methodists who side with Nellie Laidlaw form their own church, the start of South America's first large Pentecostal movement.
September
Rose Horton, Africa Inland Mission translator who helped bring the whole Bible into the Kamba language, dies in Kenya.
September
Mennonite missionary Kornelius Isaak is struck by an arrow while seeking contact with the Ayoreo people in Paraguay. He dies the next day.
September
Lutheran missionary Johann Philipp Fabricius arrives in India. He will revise the Tamil Bible and publish a Tamil hymnbook.
September
John Williams and his wife arrive on Raiatea to begin missionary work in the South Pacific.
September
Rafaravavy, a persecuted Malagasy believer, escapes to England with other Christians with help from a London Missionary Society missionary.
September
Dr. Horace Allen arrives in Korea. His care for a wounded prince wins royal favor that opens Korea to Christian work.
September
Florence Young finds assurance of forgiveness at a prayer meeting in New Zealand. She will found the South Sea Evangelical Mission.
September
P. Venkayya, evangelist on India's eastern coast, dies in Raghavapuram.
September
Joannah Ayorinde, fearless Baptist leader of the Women's Missionary Union in Nigeria, is buried in Lagos.
September
John Campanius, Lutheran missionary to the Lenape, dies.
September
Robert Moffat is commissioned with eight others as a missionary to South Africa.
September
Adano Andrew Tuye begins studies at All Nations Christian College in England. He will become the first Anglican bishop from Kenya's nomadic peoples and translate the Bible into Borana.
September
Tulinawo Msinjili, the first provincial chairman of the Moravian Church in Southwest Tanzania, dies.
September
Missionary pilot Ancel Allen is shot down over Mexico by villagers angry that he dropped gospel literature from his plane.
September
Yesaya Mwasi leaves the Livingstonia mission in Malawi to start an independent church. His principles for locally led churches spread widely.
September
Appaji Bapuji, a Brahmin convert, is baptized. He will become a missionary, translator, and pastor in India.
September
Ten Orthodox monks arrive on Kodiak Island, Alaska, to begin a mission among the Alutiiq people.
September
Lioba, who led the women of Boniface's mission to Germany, dies.
September
Thomas Lay speaks at the first annual meeting of the Medical Missionary Society in Canton, China, pledging to bring modern medicine to the world's poor.
September
Sam Sasser, missionary to the Marshall Islands and Samoa, dies.
September
Luther Rice, who rallied American Baptists to support foreign missions, dies.
September
Dr. Clara Swain sails back to India after recovering her health in America.
October
Johanna Veenstra, the first Christian Reformed missionary to Nigeria, sails from New York.
September
Honorius of Canterbury, one of the missionaries sent to England by Pope Gregory, dies.
September
Moravian missionary Friedrich Martin baptizes the first three believers among the enslaved people of St. Thomas.
September
James “Diego” Thomson of the British and Foreign Bible Society arrives in Guayaquil, Ecuador, with 800 New Testaments.
October
Mabel Dean and Hattie Salyer arrive in Egypt to begin missionary work.
October
Theophilus Solomon Schumann, Moravian “Apostle of the Arawaks” in Suriname, dies of fever.
October
James Cameron, missionary to Madagascar, dies.
October
John Hunt, missionary to Fiji, dies. Fijian believers who once opposed him beg God to take their lives instead of his.
October
John Sung sails for China after his studies in America. In fifteen years of preaching, some 100,000 people will come to faith.
October
Jonathan Udo Ekong is baptized in Nigeria. He will serve his own people for forty-six years as the Lutheran Church's first Nigerian missionary.
October
Presbyterian missionary Lucia Hammond Cozzens, teacher and writer in the Bulu language, is murdered in Elat, Cameroon.
October
Samuel Leigh opens the first Methodist church building in Australia.
October
Joseph Kiwanuka begins his training with the Missionaries of Africa in Algiers. He will become the first African Catholic bishop of modern times.
October
Carl Strehlow arrives at Hermannsburg mission in central Australia. He will translate Scripture into Aboriginal languages.
October
Edward Baierlein, Lutheran missionary to the Ojibwe of Michigan and later to India, dies.
October
Missionaries May Law and Rosa Pittman arrive in Hong Kong to help start a Pentecostal work.
October
Venezuela's government announces it will expel New Tribes Mission from the country.
October
James Lloyd Breck, called the “Apostle of the Wilderness,” begins mission and school work on the Wisconsin frontier.
October
David Brainerd, missionary to Native Americans, dies of tuberculosis at twenty-nine. His diary, published by Jonathan Edwards, inspires generations of missionaries.
October
Mary Webb gathers fourteen women into the Boston Female Society for Missionary Purposes.
October
Wilfred Grenfell, medical missionary to Newfoundland and Labrador, dies.
October
John and Charles Wesley sail for Georgia as missionaries.
October
French missionary Henri Chanès and eleven Chinese Christians are killed at Boluo, Guangdong.
October
Rainisoalambo, a Malagasy diviner, throws away his charms and turns to Christ. He will lead the “Disciples of the Lord” revival movement in Madagascar.
October
Samuel Schereschewsky dies in Tokyo. Nearly paralyzed, he typed his Chinese Bible translation with one finger.
October
Presbyterian missionary James Rodgers baptizes the first Filipino Protestants.
October
Missionary Edith Warner arrives in Lagos, Nigeria. She will serve there for decades.
October
Horace Allen, the first resident Protestant missionary in Korea, accepts an official rank so he can serve at the royal court.
October
Ann Hasseltine Judson dies in Burma at thirty-seven, worn out by her efforts to keep her imprisoned husband alive.
October
Anna Satthianadhan, who pioneered teaching Indian women in their homes, dies in India.
October
A mob in Lianzhou, China, kills six missionaries, including Dr. Eleanor Chesnut.
October
A. B. Simpson, founder of the Christian and Missionary Alliance and Nyack College, dies.
October
Protestant missionaries in Tokyo begin translating the Old Testament into Japanese.
October
P. G. Vargis arrives in Katia, India, to share the gospel. His work grows into the India Evangelical Team.
October
Christians in Japan must hand over all mission materials as a nationwide ban on Christianity takes effect.
October
North Vietnamese soldiers capture missionaries Evelyn Anderson, Beatrice Kosin, Lloyd Oppel, and Samuel Mattix in Kengkok, Laos.
October
Henry Martyn, future missionary to India and Persia, is ordained in England.
October
Hiram Bingham, Asa Thurston, and their team sail from Boston for Hawaii.
October
Pliny Fisk, missionary to Syria, dies at thirty-three, shortly before finishing an English-Arabic dictionary.
October
Former priest José Manoel da Conceição becomes a Protestant in Rio de Janeiro. He will become Brazil's leading evangelist.
November
Pliny Fisk sails for Palestine, among the first American missionaries to the Near East.
November
Missionary Arthur Tylee, nurse Mildred Kratz, Tylee's toddler daughter, and a helper are killed at a mission outpost in Brazil. Ethel Tylee survives.
November
The London Missionary Society is founded.
November
C. T. Studd meets Hudson Taylor and is accepted for service with the China Inland Mission.
November
Pan Xiushan, the first believer among the Hmu people of Guizhou, China, is killed with missionary William Fleming.
November
Barbara Johnston sails for India as Canada's first Pentecostal missionary. She will help with a Marathi New Testament before dying three years later.
October
Robert Moffat sails for South Africa, though mission leaders doubted he was qualified.
October
Samuel Schereschewsky is consecrated Episcopal bishop of Shanghai.
November
Missionaries Evelyn Anderson and Beatrice Kosin are killed by the Pathet Lao in Kengkok, Laos.
November
Henry Ballantine, missionary to India who helped translate the Bible into Marathi, dies.
November
Reuben Akinwalere George, founder of Gospel Faith Mission International in Nigeria, dies.
November
Henry Stanley finds David Livingstone at Ujiji on Lake Tanganyika, reportedly greeting him with “Dr. Livingstone, I presume?”
November
Missionary Marie Gobat calls this the hardest day of her life as she crosses the Egyptian desert with a sick child on the way to Ethiopia.
November
James Theodore Holly is consecrated bishop of Haiti, the first African American missionary bishop of the Episcopal Church.
November
Elizabeth Bowen Thompson, founder of the British Syrian Schools in Lebanon, dies. She had gone to care for widows and orphans after the 1860 massacres.
November
Joseph Mukasa, a Christian at the court of King Mwanga of Buganda who had protested the killing of Bishop James Hannington, is beheaded. He is the first of the Uganda martyrs.
November
Danish officials in India jail missionary Bartholomäus Ziegenbalg for four months, fearing his preaching will upset trade.
November
Swedish missionaries Daniel Berg and Gunnar Vingren land in Belém, Brazil. Their work grows into the Assemblies of God in Brazil.
November
The day after Joseph Mukasa's death, Denis Ssebuggwawo secretly asks missionaries in Uganda to baptize him. He will be martyred six months later.
November
Missionary nurse Bonnie Witherall, thirty-one, is shot and killed at the clinic where she served in Sidon, Lebanon.
November
The king of Warri, in what is now Nigeria, writes to the pope asking for missionaries.
November
Myra Wood writes that single women in her circle are praying and fasting so they will not be “standing here idle.” She will become a missionary to India.
November
James Evans, missionary to the Cree who created a syllabic writing system for their language, dies suddenly in England.
November
Paul Fleming, a cofounder of New Tribes Mission, dies in a plane crash.
November
Innocent of Irkutsk, Orthodox bishop who evangelized peoples of Siberia and Mongolia, dies.
November
Louise Rathke, a registered nurse and the first Missouri Synod deaconess, sails for India as a missionary.
November
Ahmed Fahmy, an Egyptian convert from Islam, is baptized in Cairo. He later studies in Scotland and serves as a medical missionary in China.
December
John G. Paton is licensed to preach. After years of city mission work in Glasgow, he will go to the New Hebrides (Vanuatu).
December
Charles de Foucauld is killed at his hermitage in the Sahara.
December
Elmon Sekgobela, a pioneer of the Nazarene work among the Tswana people of South Africa, dies.
November
Anna Breneman Haagen, missionary to the Gujarati-speaking people of India, dies.
November
Pope Gregory II consecrates Boniface as a missionary bishop to the Germans.
November
Moravian missionaries on St. Thomas welcome two enslaved believers, Andreas and Petrus, to the Lord's Table for the first time.
November
Harriet Newell, one of America's first women missionaries, dies on Mauritius at nineteen.
November
A month of revival meetings begins at Tiruvalla, India, drawing more than 100,000 a night. It gives rise to the Sharon Fellowship Church.
November
Aberi Balya, Ugandan bishop who helped translate the Bible into Runyoro-Rutooro, receives a state burial.
November
Chinese missionaries John Ding and his wife Zhu Yiming are arrested while sharing the gospel in Tibet. She dies in prison praying on her knees; he is released after twenty-three years.
November
Missionaries François Blanchet and Modeste Demers arrive at Fort Vancouver after crossing the continent.
November
African American Baptists meet in Montgomery, Alabama, to form the Baptist Foreign Mission Convention. Liberia missionary William Colley leads the effort.
November
Rebels in the Congo seize missionaries Bill McChesney and Jim Rodgers. Both are beaten to death the next morning.
November

Missionary Synnøve Mitchell asks God for a sign that her work in Pakistan matters. Days later, Bilquis Sheikh, a Muslim noblewoman, comes to her with questions about her dreams and soon follows Christ.
December
Peter Cameron Scott, founder of the Africa Inland Mission, dies of fever in Kenya before turning thirty.
December
Rowland Bingham, cofounder of the Sudan Interior Mission (now SIM), dies.
December
Medical missionary Paul Carlson, killed by rebels in the Congo, appears on the cover of Time magazine.
December
Idi Amin expels fifty missionaries from Uganda.
December
The first students of Paulo Mwamribwa, founder of the first African-led Protestant school in Tanzania's Gombero area, are baptized.
December
Channing Moore Williams, Episcopal missionary bishop to China and Japan who founded what became Rikkyo University, dies.
December
Irene Webster-Smith arrives in Japan. She will rescue young girls from the geisha trade and later share Christ with Japanese war criminals.
December
Norman Anderson, legal scholar and former missionary in the Muslim world, dies.
December
Adoniram Judson writes, “This day I made a solemn dedication of myself to God.”
December
Daniel Lindley sails from Boston for South Africa.
December
Liberian Baptists receive two churches founded by African American missionary Harrison Bouey.
December
Czar Alexander I approves a Bible Society in St. Petersburg.
December
William Carey learns that widow burning has been outlawed in India. He skips preaching that Sunday to translate the decree into Bengali at once, so no more lives will be lost.
December
Wilhelm Ringeltaube lands at Tranquebar, India. He will serve fruitfully in Travancore.
December
C. T. Studd and Stanley Smith of the Cambridge Seven speak at Edinburgh University, and many students are stirred.
December
William Henry Sheppard, African American missionary in the Congo, writes to his supporters. He will expose atrocities against the Congolese.
December
Nigerian Christians defend the record of Samuel Ajayi Crowther, the first African Anglican bishop, pointing to the thousands of conversions and many churches and schools under his leadership.
December
Johannes van der Kemp, missionary doctor to South Africa, dies in Cape Town.
December
George Pilkington, Anglican missionary and translator of the Luganda Bible, is killed in Uganda.
December
The first Moravian missionaries reach St. Thomas in the Virgin Islands.
December
Lillian Trasher, the “Mother of the Nile,” dies in Asyut, Egypt, after caring for thousands of orphans.
December
The Moravian Church in Southwest Tanzania holds its first synod at Utengule.
December
Ruth Magongo and Enoch Litswele marry. They will serve as Nazarene missionaries in several African countries.
December
Three men are ordained in Boston as missionaries to Native Americans.
December
Robert Jaffray, Christian and Missionary Alliance leader in China and Southeast Asia, is born.
December
African American Baptists organize the Lott Carey Foreign Mission Convention in Washington, DC.
December
Henry Budd becomes the first person of First Nations ancestry ordained an Anglican priest. He will serve the Cree people.
December
Japanese soldiers capture missionaries hiding in the Philippine mountains, including Signe Erickson and Erle and Louise Rounds with their children. They are killed the next day.
December
Abel Kolawole, who evangelized the Yoruba and Nupe peoples of Nigeria despite threats, dies in his nineties.
December
Evelyn “Granny” Brand dies in India after twenty-four more years of mountain ministry following her “retirement.”
December
Augustine of Canterbury baptizes thousands of Anglo-Saxons.
December
Edith Warner, missionary to Nigeria for thirty-three years, is buried.
December
Lottie Moon, Southern Baptist missionary to China, dies aboard ship in Kobe harbor, Japan.
December
Ralph and Jewyl Williams arrive in El Salvador, where they will train local believers to lead their own churches.
December
Adelaide Pollard, who wrote “Have Thine Own Way, Lord” after her plans to go to Africa stalled, dies.
December
Sattianadan Pillai is ordained, the first Tamil missionary of the Lutheran Church in India.
December
Mackay Memorial Hospital opens in Taipei, Taiwan, honoring missionary George Leslie Mackay.
December
Aaron is ordained in Tranquebar, the first Indian Protestant minister.
December
Jacob DeShazer, a Doolittle Raider who had bombed Japan, returns there as a missionary.
December
Moravian missionary Mary Hartmann dies in Suriname after carrying on the work alone following her husband's death.
December
Missionary Sidney Brooks is killed near Tai'an, China, the first foreign victim of the Boxer Uprising.
December
George Leslie Mackay arrives in Taiwan. He will plant more than sixty churches.
April
Rebels in Yarkand, China, kill Habil, a twenty-year-old Uyghur Christian teacher. Before he dies, he draws a cross and a crown on a wall: “First the cross, then the crown.”
July
Moravians celebrate fifty years of the church at Paramaribo, Suriname, where 2,477 people have been baptized.
